doc.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013

title: Using the internet to market and distribute music without a label
summary: Skype lessons, self-distribution, Prince's example, and Origin Records as a cheaper route than a label.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Okay. That’s a good answer. And I see you’re fairly — you had mentioned before having an IT person. And it looks to me like you’re fairly techno-hip. You’re offering lessons by Skype.
It’s like almost a necessity now, isn’t it.

Yeah, that’s right, that’s right, that’s right. You know I also mentioned earlier in this interview about the fact that there are ways around — not having to use a record company in order to get your music out there. That ties in with that you know. The © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

internet has become an incredible resource for musicians and we have to learn how to manipulate the internet in order to make our small business a successful one. Because as a musician you essentially are starting your own small business and you are the product. So you have to use the internet in a way of marketing/publicity, and you have to use the internet as far as getting your music out there in the way of distribution. Prior to the internet the only way you could get your music out there was to go through a distribution company, most times those distribution companies only associated themselves with record labels. If you came to a distribution company as an individual they wouldn’t even look at you because you wouldn’t have a catalogue of products to offer them. So then you looked to the record companies and tried to sign with them so you could become part of their catalogue. Well they have their own set list of criteria in order for you to get signed. So those of us who haven’t been signed onto a record label, you have to kind of fend for yourself. And then the internet comes along and you say oh wait a minute. Now we can — I can produce my own product, pay for the musician fees and get a nice package ready to go for physical distribution, and I can take that CD and also digitally upload it to my website, and also to other sites like CD Baby or there are other companies like CD Baby as well. Also divert traffic through Reverb Nation and Facebook, and have all these other sites act to divert traffic to your website so they can then find out everything about you the artist and get them interested in your music. And there are some artists that have been very successful at doing that. Prince — the R&B and soul artist — he was probably one of the first ones to really manipulate the internet early in its infancy. He had a huge record deal with Warner Brothers. And after all the success he had with “Purple Rain” —

“Little Red Corvette” and all that stuff. He said, you know I don’t have to be controlled by this big conglomerate of Warner Brothers. I can do this myself. And so he started his own record label and got a person to manipulate the internet for him, and with his name being pretty much household, he was able to draw people to his website and sell music directly through his own website and the money goes directly to him. So it is possible. And we have to figure out how to do this.
Yeah. And even some of the middle-aged jazz artists I guess I would say, who have record labels, most of them are not happy with their record labels.

Correct. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. I was just talking with a friend of mine earlier today about this, a trumpeter named Pharez Whitted. And he recently took his project to a company called Origin Records, where he can — I think you pay them a fee of about four or five thousand dollars and they’ll package your product and so you get good artwork in the packaging; they will do the publicity and the radio promo for a good maybe four to six week run, maybe an eight week run of promo; and they have international © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -11-

distribution. All for four or five grand. And those — you pay more than that, a record company, because they don’t have all that in-house so they will pay more than that for all those services. So that’s a pretty good deal. So there are ways of doing this without going the traditional route of sending in your CD to a record label with the promo kit and everything — will you sign me? So, yeah.
